items.title: Explicit infinitely divisible warm-up law and interweaving for nonlocal Jacobi semigroups
items.difficulty_reason: H2: the prior spectral expansion or one-direction bounded intertwining does not identify a probability law whose averaging reverses the operator product. The author constructs paired Markov-kernel intertwinings, computes their diagonal product as an explicit Pochhammer-ratio function of the classical Jacobi generator, uses the Bernstein inverse of the quadratic spectrum and logarithmic Pochhammer-function closure to prove complete monotonicity and infinite divisibility, and then uses injectivity rather than an assumed bounded inverse to recover the reversed product as the nonlocal semigroup averaged at the independent warm-up time. This explicit law and two-product interweaving construction are the new nonroutine core; variance, entropy, contractivity and subordination applications are supplied together without extra problem counts.

Exact Theorem2.4 operator-norm expansion/compactness/spectralmapping/selfadjointness; prior core stops before current Proposition3.21, no warm-up or entropy primary.
Actual lem:semi:hypo is a space-time DG Kolmogorov discretization energy lower bound, not an explicit random-time Markov interweaving.
Actual lem_estimD bounds a finite-volume kinetic dissipation term by projected density defects; not paired semigroups or Pochhammer warm-up transforms.
Actual lemma:commutation is an index computation for a matrix field with gradient inverse-transpose rows; no random warm-up distribution.

core_obligations: Primary is exact Proposition3.21, including original admissible m and epsilon and both root regimes
F_phi(u) uses inverse quadratic-spectrum Bernstein function rho and both Pochhammer ratios exactly as printed
Warm-up is an independent random variable and J_(t+tau) is an averaged operator, not a pathwise or deterministic-time bound
Retain both forward paired product and reversed product J_tau; cancellation uses trivial kernel, not bounded inverse
Generic entropy/hypercontractive rate depends on logS(m); optimized lambda1/2 reference choice is recorded separately from arbitrary fixed m
Keep admissible-Phi and extra Sobolev/negative-moment conditions in their own original application clauses
Subordinated spectral application has t>=1 and heatkernel has t>2 and Lebesgue-a.e. spatial scope; no all-time/everywhere upgrade
Variance coefficient optimization and direct contractivity/subordination applications are preserved uncounted; old spectral/core statements not counted again
